speaker: Doctor
text: Greeting, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin our assessment, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and does the chest pain radiate to your jaw, arm, or back?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Esophageal Rupture (Boerhaave Syndrome)

The history of persistent vomiting, forceful retching, followed by choking and sudden chest pain is classic for a rupture of the esophagus. Given the severity of the symptoms and the risk of mediastinitis, I am proceeding with urgent imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CXR_upright; REQUEST TEST: Chest_CTA_with_contrast.
